findings.title: Deep Link Token Replay — Server-Side Enforcement Not Verified
findings.attack_class: DESKTOP-MOBILE-AND-LOCAL-IPC.md#Deep-link, callback, and navigation attack classes / WEB-PROTOCOL-AND-AUTH.md#OAuth/OIDC request and callback binding
findings.trust_boundary: Google OAuth Callback (Deep Link) → Mobile App → Web Backend Token Exchange
findings.result: Replay of captured token yields valid session if web backend doesn't enforce single-use
findings.evidence: Client mints 16-byte nonce, sends to web /api/mobile/google. On callback, token from sahakarisip://auth/callback?token=... exchanged via /api/mobile/exchange. Client-side replay protection added (isHandoffTokenUsed/markHandoffTokenUsed in AsyncStorage), but comment states 'Best-effort; server enforces single-use.' Client protection is bypassable (clear AsyncStorage, different device).
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker captures token (clipboard, notification preview, browser history, compromised device). Replays to /api/mobile/exchange. If server doesn't mark token consumed, attacker obtains valid RLS JWT and accesses victim's portfolio.
findings.remediation: 1. Verify web backend marks nonce/token consumed on first exchange (idempotent rejection). 2. Add short expiry (≤5 min) to handoff tokens at issuance. 3. Consider binding token to device fingerprint (IP, user agent) at issuance. 4. Document that client-side protection is supplementary only.

findings.title: Android allowBackup="true" Exposes App Data via adb backup
findings.lower_trust_principal: Attacker with physical USB access to unlocked device
findings.affected_resource: AsyncStorage (local profiles, session, privacy settings, OAuth replay journal)
findings.result: adb backup extracts app data including financial records and auth tokens
findings.evidence: Manifest: <application android:allowBackup="true" ... android:fullBackupContent="@xml/secure_store_backup_rules">. Backup rules XML only excludes SecureStore: <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="SecureStore"/>. No exclusion for sahakarisip.v1.* AsyncStorage keys holding local profiles, session, biometric flags, OAuth replay journal.
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker with unlocked device runs 'adb backup -f backup.ab com.samimrrza.sahakarisip'. Backup includes AsyncStorage keys (sahakarisip.v1.*) and potentially SecureStore data. Local profiles, session tokens, and OAuth replay journal exposed.
findings.remediation: 1. Set android:allowBackup="false" in AndroidManifest.xml, OR 2. Create custom backup rules XML excluding sahakarisip.v1.* sharedprefs and SecureStore, reference in Manifest. 3. Test with adb backup + abe.jar extraction to verify no sensitive keys appear.

findings.title: Google Sign-In Native Path — ID Token Validation Relies on Web Backend
findings.lower_trust_principal: Attacker with valid Google ID token for victim account
findings.result: If web backend doesn't validate ID token (audience, issuer, expiry), attacker gains portfolio access
findings.evidence: Native flow: GoogleSignin.signIn() → idToken → googleNativeSignIn(idToken) → web /api/mobile/google-native. Web backend must verify ID token with Google (audience = Web client ID 416335590615-e96du..., issuer accounts.google.com, not expired). Not verifiable from this repo.
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker obtains valid Google ID token for victim (phishing, malware, stolen device). Calls /api/mobile/google-native. If server doesn't validate audience/issuer/expiry, attacker gets valid SahakariSIP session and portfolio access.
findings.remediation: 1. Verify web backend validates ID token: audience matches Web client, issuer is Google, not expired, nonce if used. 2. Ensure web backend uses google-auth-library or equivalent. 3. Log verification failures for monitoring.

findings.title: .env File with Production Credentials Exists in Working Directory
findings.lower_trust_principal: Anyone with repo access if committed
findings.affected_resource: Supabase project identifier, anon key, VAPID public key, API URL
findings.result: If committed, requires key rotation and exposes project URL
findings.evidence: .env contains EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, EXPO_PUBLIC_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, API_URL for production project. .gitignore excludes .env but file persists in workspace.
findings.attack_scenario: Developer runs 'git add .' accidentally committing .env. Anon key is public-by-design (RLS constrained) but project URL exposure aids reconnaissance. Key rotation required if leaked.
findings.remediation: 1. Delete .env from workspace; use .env.local (also gitignored) for local overrides. 2. Add pre-commit hook rejecting .env. 3. Rotate anon key if ever committed (Supabase Dashboard → API → Regenerate).

findings.title: NPM Dependency Vulnerabilities (Moderate, Transitive)
findings.lower_trust_principal: Attacker controlling input to vulnerable transitive functions
findings.result: Potential DoS via decode-uri-component; potential buffer bounds issue in uuid v3/v5/v6
findings.evidence: npm audit reports: decode-uri-component <=0.4.2 (DoS via exponential decoding) via query-string → expo-router; uuid <11.1.1 (missing buffer bounds check in v3/v5/v6) via xcode → @expo/config-plugins. Both transitive; fix requires breaking Expo upgrades.
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker provides malformed percent-encoded input to decode-uri-component (via URL parsing) causing exponential CPU. Or provides crafted buffer to uuid v3/v5/v6 causing out-of-bounds read. No direct app code calls these with attacker input.
findings.remediation: 1. Monitor for Expo SDK updates that resolve these transitively. 2. If app code directly calls vulnerable functions, add input validation. 3. Accept as low-risk transitive issues; prioritize Expo SDK upgrades when feasible.

findings.title: Profile Photo Upload — MIME Type Trust
findings.trust_boundary: User Input (File) → Supabase Storage → Browser Rendering
findings.affected_resource: Avatar serving context (potential XSS if Content-Type spoofed)
findings.result: Client validates MIME type from picker; relies on Supabase Storage to serve with correct headers
findings.evidence: updateProfileImage validates mimeType against allowlist [image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp] but mimeType comes from expo-document-picker which trusts OS/file extension. extFor derives extension from MIME type or filename. No server-side MIME sniffing or Content-Type override visible in this repo.
findings.attack_scenario: User uploads SVG with JavaScript or polyglot file with spoofed MIME. If Supabase Storage serves with attacker-controlled Content-Type, could execute in browser context when avatar viewed.
findings.remediation: 1. Verify Supabase Storage bucket 'avatars' forces Content-Type by extension or explicit policy. 2. Consider Content-Disposition: attachment for avatars. 3. Client: validate file magic bytes match expected image format before upload.

findings.title: Google OAuth Handoff — Web Backend Single-Use Token Enforcement
findings.result: Unknown — depends on web backend implementation
findings.evidence: Client relies on web backend to enforce single-use of handoff token. Web backend (sahakari-sip NextAuth) not in this repository.
findings.blocker: Web backend token consumption logic not observable in this repository.
findings.validation_plan: Owner deploys test instance, captures handoff token, exchanges twice, verifies second request fails (400/409). Verify token expiry ≤5 min.

findings.title: Supabase RLS Policies Correctly Enforce Per-User Isolation
findings.lower_trust_principal: Authenticated cloud user attempting cross-user access
findings.affected_resource: All user data tables (fund_config, entries, nav_history, notification_preferences, notifications_log)
findings.result: Unknown — depends on deployed Supabase RLS policies
findings.evidence: All cloud queries filter by user_id from JWT (RLS). Source assumes RLS policies exist: auth.uid() = user_id. Not verifiable from this repo.
findings.blocker: Supabase RLS policies are deployed configuration, not in source.
findings.validation_plan: Owner checks Supabase Dashboard → Authentication → Policies. Tests with two dummy users: sign in as user A, attempt to read user B's rows via Supabase client with user A's JWT.

findings.title: Android fullBackupContent XML Actually Excludes Sensitive Keys
findings.evidence: Manifest references @xml/secure_store_backup_rules but file content not accessible in workspace (only build intermediate found). Build intermediate only excludes SecureStore, not sahakarisip.v1.* keys.
findings.blocker: XML file content not accessible in current workspace view.
findings.validation_plan: Owner inspects secure_store_backup_rules.xml. If missing or permissive, set allowBackup="false". Functional test: adb backup + abe.jar extraction to verify no sahakarisip.v1.* keys in backup.

findings.title: Google ID Token Validation on Web Backend
findings.lower_trust_principal: Attacker with Google ID token for victim account
findings.result: Unknown — depends on web backend implementation
findings.evidence: Native flow sends ID token to web /api/mobile/google-native. Web backend must validate audience (Web client ID), issuer (Google), expiry. Not verifiable from this repo.
findings.blocker: Web backend ID token validation logic not observable in this repository.
findings.validation_plan: Owner deploys test web backend. Tests: valid token succeeds; wrong audience (Android client) fails; expired token fails; different project token fails; malformed token fails.
